title: Article 90 — Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the office of Deputy Chairman

content.overview: Article 90 provides that a member holding office as Deputy Chairman of the Council of States vacates office if he ceases to be a member of the Council, may resign by writing to the Chairman, and may be removed by a resolution of the Council passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council after at least fourteen days’ notice.
content.glance: Deputy Chairman (RS): vacates if ceases to be member; may resign to Chairman; removable by majority resolution after 14 days’ notice.
content.study:
Article 90 deals with vacation, resignation and removal of the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Removal requires a resolution of the Council passed by a majority of all the then members, with not less than fourteen days’ notice of the intention to move the resolution.

Examination: cessation of membership; resignation to Chairman; special majority and notice for removal.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Vacates office on ceasing to be a member of the Council.
2. May resign by writing addressed to the Chairman.
3. May be removed by resolution of the Council (majority of all then members) after ≥14 days’ notice.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How may the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha be removed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 90, the Deputy Chairman may be removed from office by a resolution of the Council of States passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council, after at least fourteen days’ notice of the intention to move the resolution.

examTips: Removal: majority of all then members + 14 days’ notice.

keyTakeaways: Art 90: Deputy Chairman vacation, resignation, removal (majority + 14 days’ notice).
